institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Personal connections to Vienna, academic possibilities, many different courses available at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The experience was very affected by COVID-19. The university had very strict restrictions and all events were cancelled in the winter semester. The city itself also had a lock-down and it was hard to meet new people. Many courses were online, which was very bad for making friends and also bad for getting the full outcome of the course. In the summer semester the situation got better. 
The structure of the study programmes and the course setup is very different from KU and took some time and effort to get to know. It is flexible for full degree students at BOKU, but somewhat harder to make fit when you are an exchange student from KU.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Took time but was fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Online information meeting, and we got a "buddy" assigned if we wanted - it is an austrian student who can help you with all sorts of things. Voluntary from both sides.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It is also possible to book an appointment with the ERASMUS coordinator at the host university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. Cheaper and more available than in Copenhagen. I can recommend
wg-gesucht.de

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Depends what their preferences are. I can recommend living in a shared flat, which is easy to find via
wg-gesucht.de

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to book an appointment in advance, show up in person, wait in a long line, bring documents and my own pen. It worked out, but organizational stuff in general is a lot more complicated in Austria than in Denmark.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The BOKU webpage has a lot of information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Hm, for me it was quite easy since I already had friends telling me to be early to get a place in the classes, so I signed up the first day the registration was open for most courses. It also made it easier that I had only free elective courses from KU, so I did not need to find courses fitting my mandatory courses from KU. This was a huge problem for many other students that did not manage to get a place in the courses that were mandatory, and many of the courses are overlapping at BOKU, but on purpose I chose no overlapping courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare yourself well, so you are sure you can get the courses you need.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Many courses are very small (2-3 ECTS) and they feel more like an introduction to a topic and the academic content was not so elaborate in all the courses. However, some are also more specialised and you have the chance to choose more specifically what you want. The academic content was quite varied depending on the professor. The professors structure the course and exam as they like, so they are also quite different.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
A little less for most teachers. There was a very anonymous feeling in many of the classes. You are not really on first name and active participation is not always encouraged. It was also a huge problem that there are no breaks in a 1.5 h lecture, and in a 3 hour lecture there is only one break.
In a few courses the teachers were very nice though, and encouraged students to participate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Formulation of questions and experimental design in
ecological research


831400 21W Lecture and seminar
Biodiversity crisis – climate crisis

The teachers in these courses are really nice and you are actively participating, in the first mentioned you are doing a lot of small excercises in pairs, you do a presentation and a small report, and each lecture starts with every student saying either how they feel today, what is new, or what they thought about since last lecture. The academic content helps your understanding of experimental design and be critical, plus you can learn the basic R stuff.

The second mentioned course is an individual presentation in a topic you choose, so you get to go in detail with something that interests you and it is a great challenge to be able to make a presentation in front of the class. You also need to moderate a discussion from one of the other student's presentations.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a small fee every semester, unlike in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Taking the train back and forth from Denmark to Austria is expensive, but the local transportation in Vienna is rather cheap. HOWEVER: All student discounts only apply to students under 26 years old!!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There is a very nice sport association with A LOT of opportunities - USI.
Many university events were cancelled because of COVID-19.
There is a cozy café and a bar at the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the university itself there were some lectures/movie screenings/brass band concert. In the city of Vienna there is everything culture wise you could dream of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Going to the Stammtisch for international students, brings you to different bars in Vienna and you get to know other exchange students. 
Going to the critical mass - it is a bike demonstration every third friday of the month in Vienna where you get to bike on the big car roads and the police blocks the traffic, so it is safe and very nice. Vienna is really not as good to bike in as Copenhagen, so it is important to show that we demand better bike conditions! 
Go to Donau to swim!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Karlskirche, walk the Stadtwanderweg 1a in the vineyards of Vienna, taste Kaiserschmarrn (traditional sweet dish), go for a swim in Donau, go to Leopold museum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The relationship between students and professors are not so easy to adapt to, it feels a little less friendly here. The opening hours of the university is also quite restricted and there are not so many study places available.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Austrians are very friendly!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, apart from the language of course.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are politically active and there are many small demonstrations and organizations, that is quite cool. But at the same time there is the classical culture, like all the operas, museums etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You have to plan your schedule real carefully, things are not ordered nicely in blocks and fits together in your schedule, YOU have to make everything fit, that you do not miss the mandatory activities in each course, and spend a lot of time organizing this.
2. Go to Tüwi and Stammtisch to meet people, enrol in an USI sports course.
3. Take many excursion and seminar courses and few lecture courses

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for it

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Vienna is a really nice city, especially in summer. Enjoy all the culture, events, openair cinemas, swimming in Donau.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends during lock-down and online teaching.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can warmly recommend taking the night train from Hamburg to Vienna and book the "liegewagen" for a good night's sleep and enjoy the landscape passing by outside the window :-)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
